intro: How a utility asks buildings to use less power when the grid is short. The utility's server is the VTN (virtual top node); the customer's side is the VEN (virtual end node). This lesson uses OpenADR 2.0b, the version most products in the field speak: XML over HTTPS, with the VEN polling, so the building needs no open port. The VTN says what and when; the building decides how.

poll.title: Ask for news
poll.text: At 12:00 UTC the VEN polls, as it does every minute. This time the VTN answers with an event: level 1, from 17:00 to 18:00 UTC.

optin.title: Opt in
optin.text: The event asks for an answer. The VEN opts in, and the VTN confirms.

shed.title: Shed load
shed.text: At 17:00, by its own clock, the VEN tells the building's controller to act: cooling set points go up by 2 °C and corridor lights dim. The load falls from 420 kW to 340 kW.

report.title: Report
report.text: The VEN sends the load it measures, as agreed when it registered. The utility sees the drop.

end.title: Back to normal
end.text: At 18:00 the event is over. The VEN takes its commands back, and the building returns to its schedule.

frames.tls: Open a TLS connection, with my certificate
frames.shed: Level 1 now: raise the cooling set points, dim the lights

notes.tls: The VEN always opens the connection. Both sides show a certificate issued for OpenADR. TLS 1.2, with one of the two suites OpenADR requires: TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256 or TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256.
notes.poll: An HTTP POST to /OpenADR2/Simple/2.0b/OadrPoll, carrying a small oadrPoll message: just the VEN's venID. The VTN set the poll rate when the VEN registered.
notes.distribute: The answer to the poll. It lists every pending and active event for this VEN, not only new ones. The playground shows this one line by line.
notes.created: A POST to EiEvent: an oadrCreatedEvent that names the event (eventID PEAK-20260715, modificationNumber 0), with responseCode 200 and optType optIn. optOut would tell the utility not to count on this building.
notes.response: An oadrResponse with responseCode 200. The VTN answers a poll with the same message when it has nothing new.
notes.shed: Not OpenADR: a BACnet write from the VEN to the building's controller. OpenADR only says level 1. What level 1 means is set in the building, not by the utility.
notes.update-report: A POST to EiReport: an oadrUpdateReport with a TELEMETRY_USAGE report, the building's real power every 15 minutes. The VTN asked for it with oadrCreateReport, after the VEN had registered the reports it can send.
notes.restore: Not OpenADR either. The VEN writes NULL at its BACnet priority, which releases its commands. The load climbs back to 415 kW.

a-host.name: VTN
a-host.note: The utility's server. A VTN may put a path of its own before the rest.

a-transport.name: Transport
a-transport.note: Simple HTTP. OpenADR 2.0b can also run over XMPP, where the VTN pushes.

a-profile.name: Profile
a-profile.note: 2.0b: events, reports and opt schedules. 2.0a is a smaller profile for simple devices, with events only.

a-service.name: Service
a-service.note: OadrPoll. Each message goes to its service: events to EiEvent, reports to EiReport, registration to EiRegisterParty, opt schedules to EiOpt.

facts.between: Utility or aggregator (VTN) → buildings and aggregators (VEN)
facts.transport: XML over HTTPS; the VEN polls (or XMPP)
facts.security: TLS 1.2, a certificate on each side; XML signatures optional
facts.frames: Services: EiEvent, EiReport, EiRegisterParty, EiOpt, OadrPoll

tips: Each change to an event raises its modificationNumber. Answer every new number, or the VTN thinks the VEN never got the change.
The VEN runs the event by its own clock. Keep it on NTP: a clock 10 minutes late sheds 10 minutes late.
The utility plans with every opt-in. If the building cannot shed, opt out early, not after the event has started.

playground.file: The oadrDistributeEvent of step 1, as the VEN gets it. Pick a marked line to see what it means.
playground.payload: Every OpenADR 2.0b message is an oadrPayload. The namespaces show where its parts come from: OpenADR itself, Energy Interoperation (ei), EMIX and iCalendar (xcal).
playground.signed: What an XML signature would cover. Signing is optional: TLS already protects the connection.
playground.distribute: The message: oadrDistributeEvent, from the VTN.
playground.event-id: The event's name. The VEN's answer must name it.
playground.modification: 0: the first version. Each change to the event raises it, and the VEN must answer again.
playground.market: The program the event belongs to. The building signed up to it.
playground.status: far: the event is still hours away. Later answers show it as active, then completed.
playground.test: false: a real event. A test event checks the whole chain; the VEN need not act on it.
playground.length: PT1H: it lasts one hour (an ISO 8601 duration).
playground.level: The value for this interval: 1.0. For the SIMPLE signal, 0 is normal, 1 moderate, 2 high, 3 special.
playground.simple: SIMPLE: the one signal every OpenADR VEN must understand.
playground.current: The value now: 0.0, because the event has not started.
playground.target: The event is for this VEN only.
playground.response: always: the VEN must answer with oadrCreatedEvent, opting in or out.
